drillis_contini_1966.coverage: Segment lengths and joint heights as fractions of stature H
drillis_contini_1966.notes: Population means; body-dimension definitions were not formalised by the authors. The 1972 Part II report (Contini) quotes slightly different arm ratios (0.189/0.145/0.128H); this project uses the Winter Fig. 4.1 set (0.186/0.146/0.108H) consistently.

Depth/width data other than shoulder and hip breadth

HAND_SEGMENT_PROPORTIONS: carpus / metacarpal / phalanx length split per ray, ray spacing and thumb orientation (e.g. Buryanov & Kotiuk 2010 phalangeal proportions; hand-breadth tables such as ANSUR II). NOT_ACQUIRED - the canonical hand (finding A10, docs/audit/A10_HAND_LAYOUT.md) uses PLACEHOLDER proportions 2:4:3 and 0.0133 m spacing taken from the pre-existing data, scaled to the PROVEN wrist-fingertip length (0.108 H, DRILLIS_CONTINI_1966).

FOREARM_INTEROSSEOUS_WIDTH: radius-ulna centre separation at elbow and wrist in the anatomical position. NOT_ACQUIRED - finding A11 (docs/audit/A11_FOREARM_LAYOUT.md) keeps the pre-existing PLACEHOLDER 0.0666 m separation, moved from the antero-posterior (Y) to the lateral (X) axis.

FIBULA_INTEROSSEOUS_OFFSET: tibia-fibula centre offset at knee and ankle in the anatomical position (lateral and antero-posterior components). NOT_ACQUIRED - finding A21 (docs/audit/A21_FIBULA_LAYOUT.md) keeps the pre-existing PLACEHOLDER 0.0333 m offset, moved from the anterior (-Y) to the lateral (X) axis; the posterior component is not modelled.

HIP_JOINT_CENTRE_SPACING: distance between the left and right hip joint centres (FEMUR_L/R.head). ESTIMATE - finding A23 (docs/architecture/PELVIS_HIP_CENTERS_PROPOSAL.md, variant A) sets 180.2 mm (x = +/-0.0901 m) from the BodyParts3D ratio 0.674 x inter-ASIS width 267.4 mm (one subject, internal use), Wu et al. 2002 ISB pelvic frame as geometric contrast, ANSUR II (bicristal 280.6 +/- 16.1 mm, hip breadth 351.2 mm, men 1.75-1.85 m) as plausibility control; uncertainty +/-10 mm (1 SD). A sourced regression is still pending.

SHOULDER_JOINT_CENTRE_SPACING: distance between the left and right gleno-humeral rotation centres (HUMERUS_L/R.head). ESTIMATE - finding A24 (docs/architecture/SHOULDER_GIRDLE_PROPOSAL.md, variant A) sets 406.8 mm (x = +/-0.2034 m) = ANSUR II biacromial breadth 421.1 +/- 16.8 mm (men 1.75-1.85 m, n 1814, public release) x BodyParts3D ratio GH / bone acromion spacing 0.966 (one subject, internal use); the Drillis & Contini 0.259 H ratio stays the biacromial value, not the joint spacing. Skin thickness over the acromion not modelled; +/-16 mm (1 SD).

SHOULDER_GIRDLE_LANDMARKS: sternoclavicular (SC), acromioclavicular (AC) and scapular inferior angle (AI) positions relative to the incisura jugularis and the gleno-humeral centre (ISB, Wu et al. 2005). ESTIMATE - finding A24 places CLAVICLE (SC -> AC) and SCAPULA (AC -> AI) from BodyParts3D offsets x 1.0358 (one subject); a population source is pending.

SPINE_SAGITTAL_CURVE: antero-posterior offset of each vertebral body (C1-L5) from the straight C1 -> sacrum line. ESTIMATE - Decision 71 / A26 takes the BodyParts3D body centroids (one subject, x 1.0269); shape descriptor: cervical lordosis 24.5 deg, thoracic kyphosis 42.2 deg, lumbar lordosis 24.3 deg measured as angles between centroid tangents, which are NOT Cobb angles. Qualitative pattern (cervical and lumbar lordosis, thoracic and sacral kyphosis; 7 cervical, 12 thoracic, 5 lumbar vertebrae) cited from Pro, Anatomia Clinica, ch. 2, book pp. 86-88 (no degrees given). Vertebral heights (z) unchanged; the canonical cervical spine is only 30 mm tall (finding, pending source). A sourced Cobb reference is pending.

FOOT_SEGMENT_PROPORTIONS: tarsal / metatarsal / phalanx length split per ray, heel-to-ankle offset, ray spacing and longitudinal arch profile. NOT_ACQUIRED - the canonical foot (finding A13, docs/audit/A13_FOOT_LAYOUT.md) uses the PLACEHOLDER split 3:5:3 taken from the pre-existing data, scaled to the PROVEN foot length (0.152 H, DRILLIS_CONTINI_1966); ray spacing = foot breadth (0.055 H) / 5, ankle one tarsal unit in front of the heel and a linear medial arch are ESTIMATE conventions.
